name: Peserico
why: Veneto trouser house, now dressing men too — Italian mills named on the label.
origin: Maria Peserico, Cornedo Vicentino near Vicenza, 1962 — a workshop making women’s trousers; her son Riccardo Peruffo runs it now, and the men’s collection arrived in 2021.
opview: Presents itself as Veneto tailoring tradition kept whole — an entirely Italian supply chain, from mill to final assembly.

onething.n: verified — the house was founded on trousers in 1962 and still leads with them; the men’s versions run in Loro Piana wool with a Rain System finish. Category page rather than a SKU so it survives the season

notes.wool: names its mills, which few houses do: Loro Piana, Vitale Barberis Canonico, Reda and Zegna Baruffa Lane Borgosesia among them
notes.ital: Veneto by origin and Italian end to end — Cornedo Vicentino, the Riviera del Brenta, Modena and Puglia
notes.craft: a contract manufacturer for other luxury houses before it had a label of its own
notes.style: quiet-luxury register: no logo, the cloth doing the talking
notes.reach: eleven of its nineteen US locations are concessions inside Bloomingdale’s and Saks. The map counts the eight own boutiques and not the concessions, on the rule that closed Paul & Shark
notes.tech: named weather finishes — Rain System and Green Storm System — on a line of technical wool outerwear. A real technical business sitting under a cloth-and-tailoring argument

cities: Eight own boutiques — Madison Avenue, Newbury Street, Greenwich, East Hampton, Palm Beach, Naples, Fashion Island and Stanford — plus eleven concessions inside Bloomingdale's and Saks, which the map does not count as own stores
